nodes.summary: For a right-infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and natural numbers $k$ and $i$, the length-$k$ factor of $u$ at position $i$, as a list, is $[u_i, u_{i+1}, \ldots, u_{i+k-1}]$ (the empty list when $k = 0$).
nodes.title: Factor as a list

nodes.summary: For a right-infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and a natural number $k$, the set of length-$k$ factors of $u$ is the set of the maps $\{0, \ldots, k-1\} \to \alpha$, $s \mapsto u_{i+s}$, for $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Set of factors of a given length

nodes.summary: A right-infinite word over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a sequence $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ of letters $u_n \in \alpha$. For natural numbers $k$ and $i$, the length-$k$ factor of $u$ at position $i$ is the word $u_i u_{i+1} \cdots u_{i+k-1}$, given as the map $\{0, \ldots, k-1\} \to \alpha$, $s \mapsto u_{i+s}$.
nodes.title: Factor of an infinite word

nodes.summary: If the alphabet $\alpha$ is finite, then for every right-infinite word $u$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $k$, the set of length-$k$ factors of $u$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finitely many factors of each length

nodes.summary: For a right-infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and a natural number $k$, the length-$k$ initial segment of $u$ is the word $u_0 u_1 \cdots u_{k-1}$, given as the map $\{0, \ldots, k-1\} \to \alpha$, $s \mapsto u_s$; it is the length-$k$ factor of $u$ at position $0$.
nodes.title: Initial segment of an infinite word

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a finite list of length $\ell$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and $u$ a right-infinite word over $\alpha$. Then $w$ is a factor of $u$ if and only if there is a position $i \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the length-$\ell$ factor of $u$ at position $i$, as a list, equals $w$.
nodes.title: Occurrence via list-valued factors

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, $v$ a map $\{0, \ldots, k-1\} \to \alpha$, written $j \mapsto v_j$, and $u$ a right-infinite word over $\alpha$. Then the list $[v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_{k-1}]$ is a factor of $u$ if and only if $v$ belongs to the set of length-$k$ factors of $u$. This holds also for $k = 0$.
nodes.title: Factors as lists and as tuples agree

nodes.summary: A finite list $w$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a factor of a right-infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over $\alpha$ when, writing $\ell$ for the length of $w$, there is a position $i \in \mathbb{N}$ with $w = [u_i, u_{i+1}, \ldots, u_{i+\ell-1}]$. In particular, the empty list is a factor of every right-infinite word over $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Lists occurring in an infinite word

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a finite list of length $\ell$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ a right-infinite word over $\alpha$. Then $w$ is a nonempty factor of $u$ if and only if $w$ is nonempty and there is a position $i \in \mathbb{N}$ with $[u_i, u_{i+1}, \ldots, u_{i+\ell-1}] = w$.
nodes.title: Nonempty factors via list-valued factors

nodes.summary: For a finite list $w$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ and a right-infinite word $u$ over $\alpha$, $w$ is a nonempty factor of $u$ if and only if $w$ is nonempty and $w$ is a factor of $u$.
nodes.title: Nonempty factors are the factors that are nonempty

nodes.summary: Let $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ be a right-infinite word over an alphabet $\alpha$, viewed as a map $\mathbb{N} \to \alpha$. A finite word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ over $\alpha$ is a nonempty factor of $u$ when $n \ge 1$ and there is a position $i \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $w_j = u_{i+j}$ for every $j < n$.
nodes.title: Nonempty factors of an infinite word

nodes.summary: For every infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet, the factor complexity of $w$ at length $0$ equals $1$, that is, $p_w(0) = 1$: the empty word is the only factor of $w$ of length $0$.
nodes.title: Factor complexity at length zero

nodes.summary: Let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$. For $n \ge 0$ and a position $i \ge 0$, the factor of $w$ of length $n$ at position $i$ is the word $w_i w_{i+1} \cdots w_{i+n-1}$. The factor complexity $p_w(n)$ is the number of distinct factors of $w$ of length $n$, each word being counted once however often it occurs in $w$.
nodes.title: Factor complexity of an infinite word

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
